  "text": "Her sleeve dragged through the butter on his plate.

“You've got it on your cuff,” he said.

She looked down but didn't move her hand.

“Get me the cloth.”

He stood. At the sink, the cold tap gave a knock before the water came. He wet the cloth and wrung it out carefully. When he turned back, the key was gone.

She rubbed at her sleeve.

“It'll need soap.”

“What was the number?”

“Was there a number?”

He sat down again. Beneath the table, her slippers were planted side by side, their toes touching the legs of her chair.

“I can look at the photograph myself,” he said.

“You already have.”

“The back.”

She let him take it. There was nothing on the back except a grey patch where it had once been glued into an album.

He held it towards the window. The man beside the car had one hand raised, not waving, perhaps keeping the sun from his eyes. Behind him stood a low brick wall and a gate.

“That's not a house key,” he said.

She folded the cloth into a square.

“No.”

“Then why send the address?”

“The entrance was through the house.”

He looked at the gate again. Something pale hung from its bars.

“Entrance to what?”

She reached into her cardigan pocket and put the key back beside his plate.

“Your father told me he'd returned it.”

This time she left the number showing. Seventeen.

He read it twice, then picked up the envelope to check whether there was anything left inside."
